1.why: Because speed v is squared in Ek = ½mv², doubling speed multiplies energy by four.

wrong.b: Double speed gives four times energy, not double.
wrong.d: Energy increases, it does not halve.

2.why: In Ek = ½ × m × v², letter v represents speed.

wrong.c: Voltage is V in electric circuits.

3.why: Higher speed gives much greater kinetic energy, hitting objects harder.

wrong.a: Air mass does not change much.
wrong.b: Temperature is not the main damage factor.

Which factor has its square in the kinetic energy formula?

_quiz_pool.question: What unit is used for kinetic energy?

_quiz_pool.explanation: 3 squared is 9, so energy increases 9 times.

cover.title: How fast winds pack massive energy
cover.subtitle: Storms bring powerful gusts across Indonesia. Discover why doubling wind speed multiplies kinetic energy four times.
cover.subject: Physics · Energy
cover.fun_fact: If wind speed doubles, its kinetic energy increases four times because speed is squared.
story.title: When strong winds strike
story.lead: Weather agencies issued warnings for severe wind gusts and thunderstorms [1]. Fast-moving air carries huge energy [2].
stat.1.label: kinetic energy for 1 kg of air at 5 m/s
stat.2.label: kinetic energy for 1 kg of air at 15 m/s
stat.3.label: kinetic energy for 1 kg of air at 25 m/s
story.body_1: Air is made of tiny gas particles that have mass. When warm and cool air masses clash, low pressure forms and wind starts to rush [2]. Weather warnings remind people to secure loose items outdoors before storms arrive [1].
story.body_2: Wind speed determines how much force it exerts on trees and roofs [3]. A gentle breeze feels soft, but storm-force winds can snap branches because energy grows fast as speed increases [2].
timeline.1.text: Air pressure drops and winds begin to pick up speed.
timeline.2.text: Strong gusts hammer buildings and trees with high kinetic energy.
timeline.3.text: Storm clouds move away and winds calm down.
physics.title: Kinetic energy of moving air
physics.body_1: Any moving object has kinetic energy. For wind, the energy depends on the mass of the air and how fast it travels.
physics.body_2: In the formula Ek = ½ × m × v², speed v is squared. That means doubling the speed quadruples the energy.
physics.assumptions: We assume 1 kg of air and standard wind speed vectors without friction loss.
table.note: Energy grows rapidly when wind speed increases.

lab.title: Mini Lab: Paper fan wind test
lab.step_1: Make a simple paper fan using a sheet of paper.
lab.step_2: Flick the fan gently, then wave it fast towards your hand.
lab.step_3: Feel the push of air on your hand at different speeds.
lab.question: How does waving faster change the force on your hand?
